source_text: V. Tunc Reno, qui nobiscum fuerat, somno apprehenso, ostensum est ei produci singulos, quibus prodeuntibus lucernae singulae praeferebantur; cuius autem lucerna non praecesserat, nec ipse procedebat. et cum processimus nos cum lucernis nostris, expergefactus est. et ut nobis retulit, laetati sumus fidentes nos cum Christo ambulare, qui est lucerna pedibus nostris et qui est sermo, scilicet dei. VI. Post ipsam noctem dies nobis hilaris agebatur. et continuo eadem die subito rapti sumus ad procuratorem, qui defuncti proconsulis partes administrabat. o diem laetum, gloriam vinculorum! o optata votis omnibus catena! o ferrum honorabilius atque pretiosius optimo auro! o stridor ille ferri qui strepebat dum trahitur per aliud ferrum! loqui nostrum futurorum solatium fuit, atque ne hac iocunditate tardius frueremur, a militibus incertis ubinam nos praeses audire vellet circumducti sumus huc atque illuc per totum forum. tunc nos in secretarium vocavit, quia necdum hora passionis advenerat. unde prostrato diabolo victores sumus in carcerem reversi et ad alteram victoriam reservati. hoc itaque praelio victus diabolus ad alteras se astutias vertit, fame nos et siti temptare molitus, et hoc suum praelium multis diebus fortissime gessit, ita ut (quod magis secum adversarius facere putabat) aegrorum copia ad solonem fiscalem et aquam frigidam laboraret.
thought_title: Lamps going before us and joyful chains
orientation: The imprisoned confessors writing together tell their brothers about Renus’s dream of lamps and about being dragged joyfully before the official acting for the dead proconsul and then returned to prison.
pass_a_gloss: Then, when Renus, who had been with us, had been seized by sleep, it was shown to him that single persons were being led forth, and as they were coming forth single lamps were being carried before them; but the one whose lamp had not gone before, he himself also was not going forward. And when we went forward with our lamps, he was awakened. And when he reported to us, we rejoiced, trusting that we walk with Christ, who is a lamp to our feet and who is the word, namely of God. After that very night a cheerful day was being passed by us. And immediately on the same day we were suddenly seized to the procurator, who was administering the place of the dead proconsul. O joyful day, glory of chains! O chain wished for by all vows! O iron more honorable and more precious than the best gold! O that clatter of iron which was clattering while it was being dragged through other iron! Our speaking was comfort of future things, and lest we should enjoy this delight too slowly, we were led around here and there through the whole forum by soldiers who were uncertain where the governor wished to hear us. Then he called us into the private chamber, because the hour of suffering had not yet come. Hence, with the devil thrown down, as victors we returned into prison and were reserved for another victory. Therefore, conquered in this battle, the devil turned himself to other tricks, having attempted to test us by hunger and thirst, and this battle of his he waged most strongly for many days, so that — which the adversary rather thought he was doing for himself — a multitude of sick persons was struggling with (?) fiscal solon and cold water.

pass_b_english: Then Renus, who was with us, fell asleep, and in his sleep he was shown each of us being led out one by one, with a single lamp carried before each person as he came forward; if no lamp went before someone, he did not come forward either. When we ourselves came forward with our lamps, Renus woke up. When he told us what he had seen, we rejoiced, because we trusted that we walk with Christ, who is a lamp to our feet (Psalm 119:105 (LXX 118:105)) and who is the Word of God.

After that night we spent a bright and joyful day. That same day we were suddenly seized and brought before the procurator, who was administering the place of the dead proconsul. O happy day, O glory of chains! O chain longed for with every prayer! O iron more honorable and more precious than the finest gold! O clatter of iron as it rang while iron dragged against iron! Our talking together was a comfort for what lay ahead, and so that we would not enjoy this delight too slowly, soldiers who did not know where the governor wanted to hear us marched us back and forth all through the forum. Then he called us into the private chamber, because the hour of our suffering had not yet come. So with the devil thrown down, we returned to prison as victors, kept back for another victory.

Defeated in that battle, the devil turned to other tricks and tried to wear us down with hunger and thirst, and for many days he fought this battle of his with all his force, so that, which is just what the Adversary expected to accomplish, a crowd of the sick was left struggling on the bare state ration and cold water.
notes: The clause ita ut ... ad solonem fiscalem et aquam frigidam laboraret is obscure or corrupt as given; glossed word-for-word without inventing a reading.
incertis with militibus is uncertain in sense here; glossed literally as being uncertain where the governor wished to hear the prisoners.

problems.quote: We spoke together of the comfort still to come
problems.why: The source says our talking itself was a comfort for the future. The English makes the comfort the topic of conversation.
problems.fix: Our talking together was a comfort for what lay ahead
problems.ruling: loqui nostrum solatium fuit makes speaking the comfort, not its topic

problems.quote: a crowd of the sick was left struggling on fiscal solon and cold water
problems.source_quote: aegrorum copia ad solonem fiscalem et aquam frigidam laboraret
problems.why: 'fiscal solon' is a transliteration a modern reader cannot follow. The sense is that the sick were reduced to a state-issued floor or ration and cold water. The parenthetical is also cryptic.
problems.fix: a crowd of the sick was reduced to the bare official ground and cold water
problems.ruling: 'solonem fiscalem' left as 'fiscal solon' gives no English meaning
